scheme_name: Replanting & Rejuvenation of Coconut Garden" by the Coconut Development Board
description:
The "Replanting & Rejuvenation of Coconut Garden" scheme is an initiative launched by the Coconut Development Board of India. 

This scheme was officially launched in the year 2016. 

It aims to enhance the productivity of coconut gardens across the country. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to rejuvenate old coconut palms and promote the planting of high-yielding varieties. 

The scheme targets the replanting of coconut palms that are over 60 years old. 

This initiative is crucial as older palms tend to have reduced productivity. 

The Coconut Development Board aims to increase the average yield of coconut per hectare. 

Currently, the average yield stands at approximately 6,000 nuts per hectare per year. 

The scheme aims to increase this yield to 12,000 nuts per hectare per year. 

The total area targeted for replanting under this scheme is around 1 lakh hectares. 

The scheme also focuses on improving the quality of coconut products. 

It aims to enhance the income of coconut farmers significantly. 

Farmers can receive financial assistance of up to INR 30,000 per hectare for replanting. 

This financial assistance is provided in two installments. 

The first installment of INR 15,000 is released after planting. 

The second installment of INR 15,000 is released after six months of successful planting. 

The scheme also promotes the use of high-yielding hybrid varieties. 

Farmers are encouraged to plant hybrids such as Dwarf and Tall varieties. 

These hybrids are known for their increased productivity and disease resistance. 

Eligibility for the scheme is primarily based on the age of the coconut palms. 

Farmers must have coconut palms that are at least 60 years old to qualify for replanting assistance. 

Additionally, farmers must be registered with the Coconut Development Board. 

They must also possess a valid land ownership document. 

The application process involves several steps. 

Farmers must first submit an application to the local Coconut Development Board office. 

The application should include details of the land and the age of the coconut palms. 

Farmers must also provide proof of land ownership. 

Once the application is submitted, a field verification is conducted by board officials. 

If approved, farmers will receive the financial assistance as outlined. 

The scheme operates on a continuous basis with no specific deadlines. 

However, farmers are encouraged to apply as soon as they identify old palms for replanting. 

The Coconut Development Board is responsible for implementing this scheme. 

The board operates under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

It has regional offices across various coconut-growing states. 

Farmers can contact the Coconut Development Board for more information. 

The board's official website provides detailed guidelines and application forms. 

The scheme also includes training programs for farmers. 

These programs educate farmers on best practices for coconut cultivation. 

Farmers are trained in modern agricultural techniques and pest management. 

The board also provides support for the establishment of coconut nurseries. 

These nurseries supply high-yielding hybrid seedlings to farmers. 

The scheme has seen significant participation from farmers in states like Kerala and Tamil Nadu. 

Kerala is the leading coconut-producing state in India. 

It contributes approximately 45% of the total coconut production. 

Tamil Nadu follows with around 25% of the total production. 

The scheme aims to contribute to the national goal of increasing coconut production. 

India's total coconut production is estimated at around 22 billion nuts annually. 

The scheme also supports the development of coconut-based industries. 

This includes the production of coconut oil and coir products. 

The board promotes value addition to coconut products. 

Farmers are encouraged to explore various processing techniques. 

The scheme aligns with the government's broader agricultural policies. 

It supports the vision of doubling farmers' income by 2022. 

The Coconut Development Board has set measurable targets for the scheme. 

These include increasing the area under high-yielding varieties. 

The board aims to cover at least 50,000 hectares in the first phase. 

The scheme also emphasizes sustainable agricultural practices. 

Farmers are encouraged to adopt organic farming methods. 

The board provides guidance on organic pest control measures. 

The scheme has been well-received by the farming community. 

Many farmers have reported increased yields after participating in the program. 

The financial assistance has alleviated the economic burden on farmers. 

It has enabled them to invest in better farming practices. 

The board regularly monitors the progress of the scheme. 

It conducts evaluations to assess the impact on productivity. 

Feedback from farmers is collected to improve the scheme. 

The Coconut Development Board also collaborates with state governments. 

This collaboration ensures the effective implementation of the scheme. 

The scheme has the potential to transform the coconut farming landscape in India. 

It aims to create a sustainable and profitable coconut farming sector. 

The board continues to promote awareness about the scheme. 

Workshops and seminars are conducted to educate farmers. 

The scheme is part of a larger effort to boost rural livelihoods. 

It plays a vital role in enhancing food security in coconut-growing regions. 

Farmers are encouraged to take advantage of this scheme for better yields. 

The "Replanting & Rejuvenation of Coconut Garden" scheme is a significant step towards sustainable agriculture. 

It reflects the government's commitment to supporting coconut farmers. 

The scheme is expected to have long-term benefits for the coconut industry in India. 

Farmers are urged to stay informed about the latest developments. 

The Coconut Development Board remains a key resource for farmers. 

Overall, the scheme represents a proactive approach to revitalizing coconut cultivation.
